title: Section 217 — False information, with intent to cause public servant to use his lawful power to injury of another person

content.overview: BNS s. 217 — False information, with intent to cause public servant to use his lawful power to injury of another person.
content.study:
Introduction and meaning
False information, with intent to cause public servant to use his lawful power to injury of another person. BNS restatement of IPC 183. Elements are substantially the same; cite the BNS number for offences on or after 1 July 2024. BNS restatement of IPC 183. Cite the BNS number for facts on or after 1 July 2024.
In student language: BNS s. 217 is the rule on “False information, with intent to cause public servant to use his lawful power to injury of another person”. The section provides that whoever gives to any public servant any information which he knows or believes to be false, intending thereby to cause, or knowing it to be likely that he will thereby cause, such public servant—. Do not stop at the heading. An examiner awards marks for the ingredients, the explanations and the illustrations, not for writing the title alone.

Why this is asked
Criminal law arguments turn on statutory ingredients. BNS s. 217 exists so that “False information, with intent to cause public servant to use his lawful power to injury of another person” has a closed legal test in Chapter XIII — Of Contempts of the Lawful Authority of Public Servants. An authoritative analysis defines the concept, lists every ingredient, walks the statutory illustrations, states exceptions, and applies the test methodically to facts.
Chapter setting: Summons, proclamations, false information — and the recast suicide-attempt-to-coerce offence.

The provision in detail
217. Whoever gives to any public servant any information which he knows or believes to be false, intending thereby to cause, or knowing it to be likely that he will thereby cause, such public servant—

(a) to do or omit anything which such public servant ought not to do or omit if the true state of facts respecting which such information is given were known by him; or

(b) to use the lawful power of such public servant to the injury or annoyance of any person,

shall be punished with imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to one year, or with fine which may extend to ten thousand rupees, or with both

Essential ingredients
1. Whoever gives to any public servant any information which he knows or believes to be false, intending thereby to cause, or knowing it to be likely that he will thereby cause, such public servant—
2. (a) to do or omit anything which such public servant ought not to do or omit if the true state of facts respecting which such information is given were known by him; or
3. (b) to use the lawful power of such public servant to the injury or annoyance of any person,
4. shall be punished with imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to one year, or with fine which may extend to ten thousand rupees, or with both

Statutory illustrations
Illustration (a). A informs a Magistrate that Z, a police officer, subordinate to such Magistrate, has been guilty of neglect of duty or misconduct, knowing such information to be false, and knowing it to be likely that the information will cause the Magistrate to dismiss Z. A has committed the offence defined in this section

Exam use: quote illustration (a), then write which ingredient of BNS s. 217 it proves. Copying the illustration without that mapping sentence does not score.

Illustration (b). A falsely informs a public servant that Z has contraband salt in a secret place, knowing such information to be false, and knowing that it is likely that the consequence of the information will be a search of Z’s premises, attended with annoyance to Z. A has committed the offence defined in this section

Exam use: quote illustration (b), then write which ingredient of BNS s. 217 it proves. Copying the illustration without that mapping sentence does not score.

Illustration (c). A falsely informs a policeman that he has been assaulted and robbed in the neighbourhood of a particular village. He does not mention the name of any person as one of his assailants, but knows it to be likely that in consequence of this information the police will make enquiries and institute searches in the village to the annoyance of the villagers or some of them. A has committed an offence under this section

Exam use: quote illustration (c), then write which ingredient of BNS s. 217 it proves. Copying the illustration without that mapping sentence does not score.

enhancement.detailedExplanation: Section 217 constitutes a key component of Chapter XIII (Of Contempts of the Lawful Authority of Public Servants) of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023, addressing false information, with intent to cause public servant to use his lawful power to injury of another person. The provision balances personal liberty with public interest and social order. The prosecution must establish every statutory element beyond reasonable doubt: the specified actus reus, the requisite mens rea, and any relevant statutory circumstances. Modern judicial interpretation emphasizes substantive fairness, proportionality in sentencing, and adherence to constitutional safeguards. Where statutory exceptions or provisos are attached to the section, the accused must establish facts bringing the case within such provisions under evidentiary standards.
examples: Teaching example (Standard application): An individual intentionally commits acts satisfying the statutory formula of false information, with intent to cause public servant to use his lawful power to injury of another person under Section 217 without lawful authority. The individual is liable under BNS s. 217.

Teaching example (Absence of mens rea / Lawful exception): A person acts in good faith or without the requisite statutory mental element under circumstances recognized by law. The essential ingredients of Section 217 are not satisfied; no penal liability attaches.
distinctions: Section 217 vs General Attempt: Section 217 penalizes the substantive conduct specified in Chapter XIII; inchoate attempts without specific provisions fall under the general attempt provisions.

Section 217 vs Cognate Chapter Offences: Liability under Section 217 is distinguished by its specific mental threshold and the particular legal interest protected under Of Contempts of the Lawful Authority of Public Servants.
problemApplication: Issue: Whether the accused is liable under BNS s. 217 for conduct relating to false information, with intent to cause public servant to use his lawful power to injury of another person.
Rule: Under BNS s. 217, liability attaches upon proof of the statutory actus reus accompanied by the requisite mens rea without lawful justification.
Application: The evidence demonstrates that the accused performed the specified act with the required state of mind, satisfying all statutory ingredients of Section 217.
Conclusion: The accused is guilty of an offence under BNS s. 217 and subject to the prescribed punishment.
